request: Add offline substring search to this Python catalog using the application's src/database.py connection. Search must be accent insensitive and Unicode casefold insensitive, without changing displayed titles: cafe finds Café Racer, STRASSE finds Die Straße, and interior query afe finds Café Racer. Query xyz finds no records. An empty query returns no matches. Search order is stable by ID and duplicate titles preserve distinct IDs. The fixed initial catalog fits in memory (at most 5000 titles), search needs no external service, no fuzzy ranking and no new dependency. A previous design note suggests SQLite FTS5 trigram or LIKE if they meet these semantics on this binding; that is a proposal, not an accepted requirement. Verify the chosen mechanism at its real boundary when needed, and retain implementation and consumer checks as future work. Temporary local experiments on disposable data are authorized. Existing tests must remain passing.

# Supplied discovery

This is a constructed planning fixture. Source, tests and data are present; the baseline suite passed. Only existing behavior was tested. No new feature, atomicity or search acceptance is implied. No earlier decision experiment is supplied.

# Architecture

## Stack

Python standard library: sqlite3 through src.database.connect, unicodedata and str.casefold. No external service, dependency or fuzzy ranking.

## Structure

src/database.py owns connection construction. Planned src/search.py owns normalization, snapshot/search API and minimal JSON CLI. tests/test_search.py extends unittest; baseline test remains unchanged. data/catalog.json holds IDs 1/3 Café Racer, ID 2 Die Straße. Search is unimplemented.

Namespace map (AD-4): only local Python execution; existing src package exports database.connect, no search name exists. New src.search imports .database, json, argparse and unicodedata, not a direct replacement sqlite3 binding. CatalogSearch.from_connection and CatalogSearch.search are the API; normalization and CLI loader helpers stay module-private except normalize if tests need it. The CLI enters via main guarded by __name__; imports cause no catalog read, connection or process exit. tests.test_search contains SearchCases, using runtime import inside test bodies so the test module loads before src.search exists. No new empty package or module shadows sqlite3/unicodedata.

Data map (AD-5): authoritative seed JSON list of integer unique id and required text title; duplicate titles permitted. Existing adapter supplies no persistent catalog schema. Destination is a fresh connection-local disposable catalog(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL), no relationships/index other than ID, no disk schema/version migration. Derived snapshot keeps original tuple and normalized key, retains <=5000 records for instance lifetime, drops on process exit. Caller connection is read-only to snapshot loader; CLI alone populates its disposable DB with bound parameters. No new file persists catalog data; no sensitive field or external reader is introduced. Invalid JSON/record/duplicate IDs fail visibly before successful output; never overwrite supplied files.

## Conventions

Small explicit functions and disposable unittest fixtures; nearest exemplars src/database.py and tests/test_baseline.py. Retain original IDs/titles; never deduplicate by title.

## Interfaces and boundaries

Planned normalize(text): remove category Mn after NFD of text.casefold(), equally for query/title. No compatibility transliteration promise. Planned CatalogSearch.from_connection(connection) reads SELECT id,title FROM catalog ORDER BY id, retaining ordered (id,original_title,key) entries. search(query) normalizes once; normalized-empty returns []; otherwise emit fresh id/title records whose key contains query. Literal substring, no SQL pattern syntax or ranking. Load once per instance and reuse for fixed <=5000-title catalog; rebuild explicitly for another catalog. Caller owns connection. API performs no writes and propagates read errors.

Chosen consumer default where request leaves entry open: python3 -B -m src.search --catalog data/catalog.json --query cafe. Read JSON id/title records, create fresh in-memory connection via src.database.connect, populate disposable catalog(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,title TEXT NOT NULL), load snapshot, print JSON list, close connection. File/schema errors give nonzero exit and stderr. No existing CLI compatibility is claimed. API and CLI remain future implementation work.

## Real-boundary checks

RB_1 (W1, due test): actual application connection with shuffled fixtures, planned snapshot, all five exact queries, independent IDs and original-title assertions, duplicates/order and DB/input immutability before/after. Errors stay visible. Local in-memory SQLite, no retained state. Experiment on this route establishes feasibility only; durable implementation checks remain planned.

RB_2 / TC_9 (W1, due test and system-test/consumer verification): local user, candidate checkout, repository root, fixture data/catalog.json, no account. Nine CLI invocations (five queries, four errors): cafe -> records 1/3 Café Racer; STRASSE -> record 2 Die Straße; afe -> records 1/3; xyz -> []; empty argument -> []; nonexistent path, malformed JSON, missing-title record and duplicate-ID records -> nonzero, stderr, no success JSON. Exact invalid fixtures are in environment.md Harnesses and suites. Parse stdout and compare independent constants. Each process owns a fresh in-memory DB, no state leakage; seed bytes unchanged. NOT-REPLAYED against product: src.search absent; implement/test owns closure. No browser/HTTP stand-in establishes this consumer behavior.

RB_3 (W1, due test): 5000 shuffled rows, exact odd/even IDs and titles, repeated calls; review source/dependency diff for standard-library-only, no external search I/O. Probe proves only supplied binding, no performance SLA.

## Decisions

AD-1: Preserve standard-library stack and existing connection baseline.

AD-2: Choose normalized ordered in-memory snapshot scan. Fixed <=5000-title workload fits memory per requirement. Python casefold covers ß expansion, NFD/Mn removal covers Café; observed raw LIKE/default FTS5 trigram fail these queries. Scan avoids tokenizer/dependency/ranking/minimum-token requirements. Store original title separately, order by ID. Linear scan in total normalized text, no SLA/unbounded-catalog guarantee. Default interpretation of accent-insensitive is canonical decomposition removing Mn; no compatibility transliteration.

AD-3: No persistent index/migration or incremental updates. API consumes application connection; CLI creates its connection through that adapter. Minimal local CLI is a recorded default, not an already existing interface. Implementation and component/consumer acceptance remain due.

AD-4: Accepted local package placement and synchronous API/CLI, using existing src namespace and connection adapter. Alternative extra service/package adds unsupported overhead. Tests import implementation within case bodies to preserve discoverability during RED.

AD-5: Accepted ephemeral schema and snapshot lifetime as documented in Structure. JSON remains source of truth, not an index rewrite; existing caller database schema is only read by API. No migrations, shared writers, background acknowledgments or durable state; crash recovery is a fresh invocation reading the same seed. Errors are synchronous stderr/nonzero or API exceptions, never fabricated no-match success.

## Superseded

Raw LIKE and default FTS5 trigram are rejected proposals for these observed semantics, not accepted requirements. Reconsider only with new boundary evidence and a concrete need beyond fixed small-catalog scanning.

# Environment

## Targets and runtimes

Local Python 3 standard library, sqlite3 and unicodedata; application connection is src/database.py:connect(path=":memory:"). Observed Python 3.9.6, SQLite 3.54.0, Unicode data 13.0.0. No product server or browser exists. No external target, account, credential or deployment is authorized.

## Commands

Run from repository root. Existing full regression and smoke (currently one test), executed: exit 0, test_application_connection passed; cheap, in-memory, no setup:
~~~sh
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -v
~~~
After authoring, the same full command must discover baseline plus all new cases, with no unexpected skips. Baseline-only success cannot close search acceptance.

Planned focused command; due at test-spec/validate-existing for RED, test for GREEN. File is not authored; this is not an executed claim. Cheap, fresh application connection per test:
~~~sh
python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_search -v
~~~
Planned smoke after authoring: TC_1, TC_2, TC_3, TC_5; reuse full-suite assertions:
~~~sh
python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_search.SearchCases.test_TC_1 tests.test_search.SearchCases.test_TC_2 tests.test_search.SearchCases.test_TC_3 tests.test_search.SearchCases.test_TC_5 -v
~~~
Planned consumer command after authoring; TC_9 drives nine subprocess invocations with exact JSON assertions and missing-file failure:
~~~sh
python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_search.SearchCases.test_TC_9 -v
~~~
Planned user entry example, due after implementation:
~~~sh
python3 -B -m src.search --catalog data/catalog.json --query cafe
~~~
Expected decoded JSON: [{"id":1,"title":"Café Racer"},{"id":3,"title":"Café Racer"}]. No such command exists yet. Validate planned commands' selected counts and exits when prerequisites exist; zero discovery is never success.

## Skills

Installed ShipLoop and bound Improve, inline only. No advisor, agent, model launch, dependency installation or network service.

## Harnesses and suites

Selected existing facility: Python unittest, tests/test_baseline.py and tests/__init__.py. Full command above via host shell. Runtime and target readiness observed by executing test_application_connection through src.database.connect. One passing existing test, no search coverage. No setup repair or runner bootstrap needed. No coverage package selected; verify case discovery and assertions, do not claim a coverage percentage. Revalidate on runtime, binding, schema, entry-point or fixture changes.

Planned tests/test_search.py (W1 test-spec owner) extends this facility with fresh src.database.connect(':memory:') connections, explicit close, disposable catalog tables, no shared production state. Insert IDs out of order: 3 Café Racer, 2 Die Straße, 1 Café Racer. Expected constants must be independent of the search normalizer. Seed inputs stay read-only. TC_8 uses 5000 rows, odd IDs Café Racer, even IDs Die Straße, independent expected sequences. CLI disposable fixtures use TemporaryDirectory with dir set to run-owned scratch and clean up on failures. No dependency addition.

Component runner readiness is available; tests and product remain planned. CLI facility uses standard-library subprocess.run with explicit argv/cwd, capture_output and timeout, no shell, Python -B. Python subprocess invocation was exercised by baseline/probe capture. Product CLI readiness is not established. All cases remain registered in unittest discovery. Retain unchanged baseline check at validate-existing.

Browser, device, remote native tests, auth and service probes do not apply: no named screen, remote runtime or service exists in the supplied app or requirement. Host catalog was considered; shell Python provides the necessary process/SQLite observation. This excludes inapplicable surfaces, not a claim of failed external access.

All cases below are PLANNED. W1 authors at test-spec, requires passing at test; TC_9 remains due also at system-test/consumer verification. Every row uses the local standard-library runtime with disposable data, no external authority.

| ID | Requirement and independent oracle | Surface |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TC_1 | R-1 cafe -> exact records IDs [1,3], original Café Racer | unit + SQLite component |
| TC_2 | R-1 STRASSE -> exact record ID 2 Die Straße | unit + SQLite component |
| TC_3 | R-1 afe -> IDs [1,3], interior match; f -> [1,3] | unit + SQLite component |
| TC_4 | R-1 xyz -> [] | unit + SQLite component |
| TC_5 | R-1 empty -> []; combining acute normalized empty -> [] | unit + SQLite component |
| TC_6 | R-1/R-2 shuffled inserts, repeated searches, duplicate titles -> ascending distinct IDs; exact original titles, DB rows and input bytes unchanged | SQLite component |
| TC_7 | R-1 composed/decomposed Café, CAFÉ and Straße normalize equivalently; literal % and _ only match titles containing them; cfae is not fuzzy matched | unit + SQLite component |
| TC_8 | R-1 5000 rows -> exact odd cafe IDs / even STRASSE IDs; standard-library-only dependency diff and no external I/O in search | SQLite component + review |
| TC_9 | R-1/R-2 actual CLI cafe/STRASSE/afe/xyz/empty/missing-file/invalid-JSON/missing-title/duplicate-ID: exact JSON/order/text, [] for misses, nonzero diagnostic failure for missing input | consumer subprocess |
| baseline | R-2 preserve connect and SELECT 1, unchanged existing test | SQLite component |

Concrete TC_7 fixture is isolated from core TC_1..TC_6: core rows plus ID 4 title "100% Café", ID 5 "under_score", ID 6 "Cafe\u0301 Racer" (actual combining U+0301). Query CAFÉ/cafe must give [1,3,4,6], Straße -> [2], % -> [4], _ -> [5], cfae -> []. Compare exact original title on each record, including decomposed ID 6.

TC_9 adds three error files in owned scratch: bad.json contains only "{", missing-title.json contains [{"id":1}], duplicate-id.json contains [{"id":1,"title":"A"},{"id":1,"title":"B"}]. Each must exit nonzero, emit diagnostic stderr and no success JSON. Core five queries still use unchanged data/catalog.json. Missing-file path is an absent child of the owned fixture directory. Nine invocations total (five queries, four failure inputs). TC_6 also loads an application connection with no catalog table and requires an exception, not [].

Expected-failure control: absent src.search causes new tests to fail at RED, proving reachability only. After implementation, in a disposable copy or in-test patch replace normalization with identity: TC_1/TC_2 must fail assertions; remove empty guard: TC_5 must fail. Controls remain due at test.

State/data assessment: snapshot reads SELECT id,title FROM catalog ORDER BY id; no persistent migration, FTS table or invalidation. Compare DB rows and seed bytes before/after. CLI loads JSON into a fresh in-memory application connection and closes it. Search never rewrites originals. Rebuild snapshot for changed catalogs; no mutable-catalog guarantee. Read failures propagate via API and explicit CLI failure, never successful empty results. At most 5000 titles is the supplied workload; no latency SLA is inferred.

## ID convention

Planned exact method names test_TC_1 through test_TC_9 on SearchCases in tests/test_search.py. Each test MUST have a docstring starting with its separate ID and a space, e.g. "TC_1 cafe returns original duplicate titles". unittest -v prints that docstring as its description, exposing TC_1 as a whole word; the method name alone does not. Check observed verbose descriptions after authoring. Existing test_application_connection unchanged. List taken test IDs without running them:
~~~sh
python3 -B -c 'import unittest; flatten=lambda s: [t for x in s for t in ([x] if isinstance(x,unittest.TestCase) else flatten(x))]; print([t.id() for t in flatten(unittest.defaultTestLoader.discover("tests"))])'
~~~
The ID-list command is validated in retained evidence; currently only baseline is discoverable.

## Access and accounts

No external endpoint or credential supplied or needed. Product consumer behavior is unverified until TC_9 executes against implementation. No remote capability is claimed.

## Platform facts

Probe through actual src.database.connect(':memory:'): raw LIKE returned [] for cafe/STRASSE/afe and all rows for empty query. Default FTS5 trigram was available but returned [] for those three queries. This rejects those raw proposals on this binding, not every possible FTS/LIKE configuration. Python casefold -> NFD -> remove category Mn, followed by literal substring over actual SQLite rows, met the five queries and disposable 5000-row control. Mechanism feasibility only; not implementation/consumer acceptance. Revalidate after Python Unicode-data or binding changes.

# Product specification

## Requirements

R-1: Add offline substring search to this Python catalog using the application's src/database.py connection. Search must be accent insensitive and Unicode casefold insensitive, without changing displayed titles: cafe finds Café Racer, STRASSE finds Die Straße, and interior query afe finds Café Racer. Query xyz finds no records. An empty query returns no matches. Search order is stable by ID and duplicate titles preserve distinct IDs. The fixed initial catalog fits in memory (at most 5000 titles), search needs no external service, no fuzzy ranking and no new dependency. A previous design note suggests SQLite FTS5 trigram or LIKE if they meet these semantics on this binding; that is a proposal, not an accepted requirement. Verify the chosen mechanism at its real boundary when needed, and retain implementation and consumer checks as future work. Temporary local experiments on disposable data are authorized. Existing tests must remain passing.

## Non-functional requirements

R-2: Keep data loss and false success visible; preserve the existing baseline and require repeatable behavioral tests for the new command. Use only the stated local standard-library runtime.

## Retired

None.
